summary: Green Knob, Clark County WA: 1942 smokehouse or wartime cabin (sources disagree), DNR tower 1960, removed or destroyed 1974; parts reported near the summit behind a permit gate.

facts.design: Two-story 10x10 'smokehouse' (1942) per FFLOS and firelookout.com, disputed by WillhiteWeb; 20-foot wooden DNR tower (1960)
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1974 (sources differ on the word). WillhiteWeb reports lookout parts and anchor bolts near the summit.

access.note: Weyerhaeuser permit area, reached by a gated road off Forest Road 54, per WillhiteWeb

visit.trail_note: The gated road runs to within about 200 feet of the summit, per WillhiteWeb. WillhiteWeb lists a hiking and biking distance of 8.5 miles one way on a non-motorized permit.

events.note: Two-story 10x10 'smokehouse' per FFLOS and firelookout.com; WillhiteWeb disputes this (see resolved conflicts)

FFLOS says removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; WillhiteWeb says the Lookout Inventory suggests destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com describe a two-story 10x10 smokehouse built in 1942. WillhiteWeb's note says the DNR did not follow through on a lookout in 1942-43, and that a 14x32 portable cabin was built in its place. The story reports both.
FFLOS and firelookout.com give 20 feet for the 1960 tower. WillhiteWeb gives 20 or 40 feet, and the August 1969 article describes the tower as 40 feet before its planned shortening to 10.
FFLOS gives 2,300 ft (701 m), which matches the brief's record. WillhiteWeb gives 2,964 feet. The story does not state an elevation.
FFLOS says the tower was removed in 1974. firelookout.com says it was destroyed that year, and WillhiteWeb says its Lookout Inventory suggests the same. The story reports both words.

sources.title: Green Knob, Forest Lookouts (quoting The Oregonian, August 1969)

notes_for_editor: Read the four source pages, two of them more than once, so about 6 reads counting repeats, and ran 1 web search. Today's condition rests on WillhiteWeb's visit notes, which are undated; its access section lists the gated permit road. The first structure is disputed between FFLOS and WillhiteWeb, and the story says so. The brief's elevation_m 701 matches FFLOS but not WillhiteWeb (2,964 ft). No corrections proposed; the brief's kind 'tower' fits the 1960 structure.
